findings.title: New startup validator aborts with an uncaught ValidationError traceback for configs that loaded before
findings.problem: validate_url_ssrf now runs on every InstanceConfig built from triggarr.toml, including disabled instances. The startup path, ensure_config() in triggarr/config.py:370-373, catches only TOMLDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError, and its docstring at line 345 says pydantic.ValidationError keeps propagating uncaught. A hand-edited config that loaded fine before this change will now crash at startup with a raw traceback instead of the friendly message plus exit(1) that _log_corrupt_config_and_exit gives. Two examples: a disabled instance with url = "radarr:7878" (no scheme, so urlparse reads 'radarr' as the scheme), or a URL with a malformed IPv6 bracket. Under Docker's restart policy this becomes a crash loop. Rejecting disabled instances is documented as intended (D-01/D-02), so the finding is the unfriendly, unhandled failure path, not the rejection itself. pending: confirm no handler above ensure_config (in main/_run) catches ValidationError and logs it.
findings.fix_hint: catch pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config/load path and log a friendly per-field error naming the instance + sys.exit(1), mirroring _log_corrupt_config_and_exit
findings.why_it_matters: On upgrade, existing users with a stale or malformed URL on an instance they don't use get a container that won't start and only a traceback to diagnose it.

members.title: Config model layer now depends on the web package for URL validation
members.problem: Before this change, triggarr/models/config.py imported nothing from inside triggarr. It was a leaf that 9 production modules import, including db.py, state.py, search/engine.py and startup.py. The new validator makes it depend on triggarr/web/validation.py, so the config schema now relies on the UI layer, and anything that loads InstanceConfig (the scheduler, the CLI, tests) also pulls in triggarr.web. I checked for an import cycle and there isn't one: web/__init__.py is empty and validation.py imports only stdlib (ipaddress, re, urllib.parse). That means the function-local import isn't needed to avoid a cycle. It only hides the dependency. The codebase does already tolerate one lower-layer-to-web lazy import (triggarr/search/scheduler.py:532 and :538 import from triggarr.web.routes), so this is not a clear break from an established layering rule. pending: confirm whether the project means to keep models/ free of web/ dependencies.
source_window: Raises ValueError on violation so Pydantic surfaces a ValidationError.
members.why_it_matters: The config model sits at the bottom of the dependency graph. If it starts depending on the web package, a later change to web/validation.py (for example, adding a FastAPI or loguru import) could quietly add an import cycle or slow down every non-web consumer. It also makes it harder to find where SSRF policy lives.
members.fix_hint: Move the stdlib-only URL/SSRF helpers (BLOCKED_HOSTS, _BLOCKED_NETWORKS, validate_arr_url, validate_arr_url_config) into a neutral module such as triggarr/net_validation.py or triggarr/models/url_validation.py. Have both models/config.py (top-level import) and web/routes.py import from it, and leave web/validation.py for form helpers only.

members.title: Startup ValidationError for a URL with credentials goes to stderr unredacted, bypassing the loguru redacting sink
members.problem: When this validator raises during startup, pydantic's ValidationError includes input_value=<full url>. Because ensure_config doesn't catch it, the traceback goes to stderr through sys.excepthook rather than the redacting loguru sink. A URL carrying userinfo (http://user:pass@host) or other secret-bearing parts would therefore be printed in the clear. The apikey= validator just above already has the same exposure. pending: confirm no top-level handler routes uncaught exceptions through loguru, and confirm whether userinfo URLs occur in practice.
members.why_it_matters: Credentials embedded in a URL could end up in container logs.
members.fix_hint: handle ValidationError at the startup boundary and log only field location + error msg, not input_value

members.title: New config-load SSRF validator inherits helper's documented DNS-rebinding / non-canonical-IP gap
members.problem: This diff wires validate_arr_url_config (an existing, unchanged helper in triggarr/web/validation.py, added in the prior commit) into InstanceConfig.url at config-load time. The helper's own docstring already discloses that hostnames are never DNS-resolved at validation time, so a hostname that currently resolves to a public/allowed address but is rebound to 127.0.0.1 or another blocked address at request time would pass this new validator and still be blocked-address-free at config load. Non-canonical IPv4 literal forms (decimal/octal/hex) that some resolvers normalize to a blocked address are similarly unexamined by ipaddress.ip_address() and fall through to the unresolved-hostname branch. This is purely a pre-existing property of the helper being extended to a new caller, not a weakening introduced by this diff's own changed lines.
source_window: Raises ValueError on violation so Pydantic surfaces a ValidationError.
members.why_it_matters: If exploitable, a config-supplied *arr URL could reach an internal or metadata service despite passing validation, but this requires control over triggarr.toml (a different, higher-privilege trust boundary than the HTTP settings form) and the gap already exists for every other caller of this helper.

members.title: Relaxed SSRF helper misses alternate encodings of metadata hosts (pre-existing helper gap)
members.problem: This diff tightens checks and routes the URL through validate_arr_url_config (triggarr/web/validation.py:111). That helper's unchanged logic lets several metadata-host encodings through. (1) A trailing-dot FQDN such as http://metadata.google.internal./ is not in BLOCKED_HOSTS. (2) Decimal or short-form IPv4 such as http://2852039166/ fails ipaddress.ip_address() and is treated as a hostname, though getaddrinfo may resolve it to 169.254.169.254. (3) Plain IPv4 in 100.64.0.0/10 other than 100.100.100.200 is checked only in the IPv4-mapped form, not as a bare IPv4 literal. The strict validate_arr_url has the same gaps, so this is pre-existing. pending: demonstrate httpx resolving the decimal/trailing-dot form to the metadata IP.
members.why_it_matters: The documented goal is to always block cloud-metadata addresses, and these encodings slip past that.
members.fix_hint: normalize hostname (rstrip('.'), lower) and reject non-dotted-quad numeric hosts; apply _BLOCKED_NETWORKS to plain IPv4 too

members.title: Startup ValidationError output includes the raw URL, which can carry userinfo credentials
members.problem: When this validator raises, pydantic's ValidationError string contains input_value=<full url>. At startup that error propagates uncaught, so the traceback goes to stderr instead of through the loguru redacting sink. A URL such as 'http://user:pass@169.254.1.1' would print its basic-auth credentials to the container logs. The same exposure already exists through reject_apikey_in_url. This diff only adds more rejection cases that reach it. pending: confirm that stderr tracebacks skip the redacting sink, and that userinfo URLs occur in practice.
members.why_it_matters: The project's security convention says secrets never appear in logs.
members.fix_hint: Handle ValidationError at the ensure_config boundary and log only field location and message, not input_value
